Apex Manufacturing — Procurement Policy
 Document ID: POL-PROC-001  |  Version 3.2  |  Effective: January 15, 2025
1. Purpose and Scope
This policy governs the procurement of all materials, components, and services used in manufacturing
operations at Apex Manufacturing. It applies to all purchase orders, supplier agreements, and
procurement decisions across all product lines and facilities.
2. Approved Supplier Requirements
All procurement must be from suppliers listed on the Approved Supplier List (ASL). The ASL is
maintained by the Quality Assurance department and reviewed quarterly. Suppliers that have been
removed from the ASL may not be used under any circumstances, regardless of pricing or availability.
2.1 Supplier Certification
Suppliers of electronic components, printed circuit boards, and safety-critical parts must hold current
ISO-9001 certification. Suppliers of power supply components (capacitor banks, transformer cores)
must additionally hold UL listing certification. Certification status is verified annually.
3. Domestic Sourcing Preference
Apex Manufacturing prefers domestic (United States and Canada) suppliers for all components.
International suppliers may be used when: (a) no domestic supplier can meet required delivery
timelines, (b) the domestic price premium exceeds 35% of the international price, or (c) the component
is not available from any domestic source. Justification for international sourcing must be documented
in the purchase order rationale.
Note: For components classified as 'critical' (defined in Section 6), the domestic price premium threshold is
50% rather than 35%.
4. Supplier Concentration Limits
To mitigate supply chain risk, no single supplier may account for more than 70% of the total volume of
any critical component within a rolling 12-month period. For non-critical components, the concentration
limit is 85%. The procurement team must maintain at least two qualified suppliers for every critical
component.
 
Exception: Where only one supplier exists globally for a specialized component (sole-source), a Sole
Source Justification must be documented in the purchase order rationale.
4.1 Minimum Order Quantities
Purchase orders must meet the supplier's stated minimum order quantity (MOQ). Orders below MOQ
require written supplier approval.
5. Hazardous Materials
All hazardous materials (as classified in the component database) require special receiving and
handling procedures and must be stored in the designated Hazmat Storage area. Orders for hazardous
materials should be flagged for procurement review, as these materials are subject to additional
receiving requirements that may extend delivery timelines. FIFO (First In, First Out) rotation is strictly
enforced.
6. Critical Components
The following component categories are classified as critical: microcontroller ICs, power MOSFETs,
PCB blanks, neodymium magnets, and all sensor ICs (temperature, pressure, humidity). Critical
components are subject to enhanced sourcing requirements including tighter concentration limits
(Section 4) and higher domestic price premium thresholds (Section 3).
7. Budget and Cost Controls
All procurement decisions must consider total cost of ownership, including unit price, shipping, and
handling costs. Orders exceeding $50,000 require Procurement Manager approval. Orders exceeding
$150,000 require VP of Operations approval.
7.1 Emergency Procurement
Emergency purchase orders (required to prevent production stoppage) may bypass standard approval
thresholds up to $75,000, but must be documented with a rationale and approved retroactively within 5
business days.
8. Sustainability Requirements
When selecting between suppliers with comparable pricing (within 10%) and delivery timelines (within 5
business days), preference should be given to suppliers with a sustainability rating of A or higher.
Suppliers with a sustainability rating below B are subject to additional review and should only be used
when no alternatives are available.
Suppliers holding ISO-14001 certification receive preferential consideration.
 
9. Strategic Supplier Relationships
Suppliers designated as 'Strategic' tier represent key long-term partnerships. The procurement team
should maintain consistent order volumes with Strategic suppliers to preserve relationship stability,
even when short-term alternatives offer moderately better pricing (up to 15% savings). Decisions to
shift significant volume away from Strategic suppliers require VP of Operations approval.
10. Shipping and Lead Times
Purchase orders should be placed with sufficient lead time to ensure materials arrive before the
scheduled production start date. The supplier catalog lists standard lead times for each component.
International suppliers typically ship via ocean freight; expedited air freight may be authorized by
management memo when schedule demands require it. The expected delivery date on each purchase
order must reflect the supplier's quoted lead time from the date of order.

APEX MANUFACTURING — INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
Memo ID: MEMO-2025-041
Date: April 15, 2025
From: Sandra Chen, VP of Operations
To: All Procurement Staff
Subject: Updated Supplier Concentration Limits for Rare Earth Components
Following the recent supply disruptions in Q1 2025 related to rare earth material shortages, I am
issuing updated guidance on supplier concentration limits for neodymium magnets and related rare
earth components.
Effective immediately, the supplier concentration limit for neodymium magnets (RM-3003) is reduced
from 70% to 50% for any single supplier. This supersedes the general critical component concentration
limit stated in Procurement Policy Section 4.
Additionally, all purchase orders for neodymium magnets must include a secondary supplier allocation
of at least 20% of the total order volume. This applies even when the secondary supplier has a higher
per-unit cost.
The procurement team should work with MagnetPro Inc. (SUP-108) to increase their qualified capacity
for N52-grade magnets. Until MagnetPro's capacity is confirmed sufficient, Nanjing Rare Earth Co.
(SUP-107) remains our primary volume supplier, but orders must be structured to meet the new 50%
concentration cap.
Please update all open and future purchase orders accordingly. Questions should be directed to the
Procurement Manager.

APEX MANUFACTURING — INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
Memo ID: MEMO-2025-072
Date: July 1, 2025
From: David Park, Procurement Manager
To: Procurement Team, Production Planning
Subject: Temporary Authorization for Expedited Shipping from International Suppliers
Due to increased customer demand in Q3 2025, I am temporarily authorizing the use of air freight for
international supplier shipments where ocean freight lead times would cause production delays.
Effective July 1, 2025 through September 30, 2025, international suppliers may be asked to ship via
air freight at Apex Manufacturing's expense. When air freight is used, the effective lead time for
international suppliers is reduced by 14 days from their standard catalog lead time (but not below 7
days minimum).
Air freight authorization is limited to components needed for confirmed production orders. Speculative
or safety-stock orders do not qualify for air freight.
The additional cost of air freight (estimated at $8-12 per kg) should be documented on the purchase
order. Total air freight expenditure is capped at $25,000 for the authorization period. The Procurement
Manager must approve each air freight request individually.
This authorization does not override any other procurement policy requirements including supplier
certification and hazardous materials handling.

APEX MANUFACTURING — INTERNAL MEMORANDUM
Memo ID: MEMO-2025-085
Date: August 20, 2025
From: Maria Santos, Quality Assurance Director
To: Procurement Team, Production Planning, Electronics Assembly
Subject: Enhanced Quality Requirements for PCB Components
Following the identification of micro-cracking issues in two recent PCB lots, I am implementing
enhanced quality measures for all printed circuit board components (RM-3005) effective immediately.
New requirements (effective August 20, 2025):
1. PCB suppliers must provide a Certificate of Conformance (CoC) with each shipment including
cross-section analysis results. Shipments without a CoC will be rejected at receiving and returned to
the supplier.
2. Until further notice, we are suspending new supplier qualification for PCB components. Only
suppliers from whom we have previously received and accepted PCB shipments may be used. If a PCB
supplier is new to us, we cannot order PCBs from them at this time.
These measures will remain in effect until the root cause investigation is complete and corrective
actions are verified, estimated 60-90 days.
